title: Outdoor Irrigation, Rainfall and Seasonal Water Demand

content.overview: Outdoor irrigation should respond to plant demand, rainfall, soil water storage, planting density and delivery efficiency. Research in field hemp shows irrigation response is context dependent, so fixed gallons-per-plant rules should not be treated as universal.

vocabulary.definition: Combined loss of water through soil evaporation and plant transpiration.
Rainfall that is retained in the root zone and available to the crop.
Low-volume irrigation delivered near the root zone through emitters or drip lines.

sections.title: Demand changes through the season
sections.body: Plant size, weather and reproductive development alter water use. Irrigation scheduling should therefore be updated as the crop and environment change.

sections.title: Rainfall must be interpreted, not just counted
sections.body: A rain event may wet the surface without fully recharging the root zone, while heavy rain can create excess moisture or drainage problems. Soil moisture and crop response show how much of the rainfall was actually useful.

sections.title: Delivery method changes disease and efficiency context
sections.body: Drip can reduce canopy wetting relative to overhead irrigation and place water near the active root zone, but layout and maintenance still determine uniformity.

workedExamples: After a brief summer shower, check soil moisture before canceling irrigation automatically.
If end-of-line plants receive less water, inspect pressure and emitter uniformity before diagnosing nutrition.
commonMistakes: Using the same irrigation volume from establishment through harvest.
Treating every rainfall amount as fully available water.
content.practicalApplication: Track rainfall, irrigation volume, soil moisture or plant water-status indicators, crop stage and weather. Adjust frequency and amount from measured response rather than a fixed seasonal recipe.
content.summary: Outdoor irrigation is a water-balance problem. Rainfall, crop demand, soil storage and delivery uniformity should be interpreted together.
